lesson.title: Final Devoicing Gym
lesson.subtitle: hond/honden, huis/huizen, stad/steden — hear the change, keep the letter

hook.title: The Letter That Comes Back
hook.content: Dutch final devoicing is not a spelling mistake; it is a sound rule with a spelling repair. The singular may sound voiceless, but the plural tells you which letter belongs there.

pattern.title: Singular sound, plural spelling
pattern.content: Compare hond and honden, huis and huizen, stad and steden. The plural restores the voiced consonant, so the singular spelling keeps it too.
pattern.trap_note: The rule applies to the sound, not the letter: final d and b devoice, but Dutch still writes d and b.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Final Devoicing Gym):
exercises.target_answer: geel, het jaar, goed, de hond, de stad, het huis
exercises.meaning: yellow, year, good, dog, city, house
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Final Devoicing Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “The dog is small.”?
exercises.explanation: “De hond is klein.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Final Devoicing Gym”.

cues: The pattern: Singular sound, plural spelling
It means: The dogs are big.
exercises.explanation: “De honden zijn groot.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Singular sound, plural spelling.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: The rule applies to the sound, not the letter: final d and b devoice, but Dutch still writes d and b.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Het huis is geel.” is word-for-word “The house is yellow.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Singular sound, plural spelling.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The year is long.
exercises.explanation: “Het jaar is lang.” reuses only material taught in “Final Devoicing Gym” — Singular sound, plural spelling.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Het jaar is lang.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Singular sound, plural spelling.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “The city is old.”
twist.explanation: The singular sounds like 'stat', but the plural steden proves the d.

summary.outcome: Apply final devoicing without corrupting the spelling of Dutch nouns.
summary.takeaway: Dutch spelling is a record of the word's family, not a phonetic transcript.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Zijn & Hebben.

geel.etymology_derivation: English yellow and Dutch geel are cognate; English y answers to Dutch g here.

jaar.etymology_derivation: English year and Dutch jaar are the same word; both take a y/j, not a g.

goed.etymology_derivation: English good and Dutch goed are the same word.

hond.etymology_derivation: English hound and Dutch hond are the same word; the final d devoices.

stad.etymology_derivation: English stead and Dutch stad are the same word; Dutch narrowed it to city.

huis.etymology_derivation: English house and Dutch huis are the same word; ui answers to ou.
